concepts.name: Pika
concepts.details: Specific design PIKA: a short plump capsule with a blunt rounded snout and a gently rising turtle-shell roof, about 12.5 m long by 5.5 m wide, only one inhabitable deck. Think a beautifully practical deep-space camper, not a bus. Small inset three-pane cockpit at the low front, a broad curved ivory body widening around the snug living compartment, one square blue-trimmed hab porthole along the side. Rear quarter contains the small hold and a SIDE loading ramp visible on the camera-facing rear flank. Two restrained drive bells tucked tightly into recessed rear corners, tiny dark radiator grilles integrated on the back. Four short articulated landing legs with broad pads. Cream hull with substantial dusty cobalt-blue lower panels and just two muted ochre hardware accents. Fine mechanical detail clustered around hatch hinges, RCS and maintenance access; leave big calm curved hull panels. Show front-left three-quarter, open side ramp showing only two racks just inside. It should read as a compact endearing practical home from silhouette alone.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: individual exterior ship concept for a cozy first-person space-hauling game. One complete landscape illustration, not a contact sheet.
Primary request: design one SMALL COMPACT STARTER UTILITY HAULER, an affordable one-person working spacecraft that is also a tiny home. Practical cassette-futurist hardware, a cockpit with physical CRT instruments glimpsed through modest windows, enclosed pressurized living space for a bunk/galley/tiny washroom, a small enclosed cargo hold for hand-carried boxes, accessible ramp, discrete reaction thrusters, real landing feet, plausible engine and fuel placement. The cargo hold is modest, NOT stacks of shipping containers. Use the hull volumes economically, with headroom for walking inside.
Style/medium: Moebius-inspired European science-fiction graphic novel illustration, clean fine dark-blue ink contours with selective panel lines, broad quiet gouache color fields, subtly painterly edges, restrained paper texture. Rounded, bevel-edged manufactured forms and analog industrial details. The illustration must feel like the exterior counterpart of our approved warm cream and blue illustrated spaceship hab. Warm golden illumination, clear hard-edged blue-violet cast shadows, matte painted metal, sparse believable wear. No photoreal rendering, no gritty PBR, no anime fighter, no thick cartoon outlines, no voxel blocks.
Composition: a clear three-quarter exterior view, slightly elevated enough to see the roof, whole spacecraft and landing feet uncropped with generous margin. Ship fills about 75 percent of landscape frame. A simple quiet station apron with a few seam lines, a pale muted background; avoid a busy hangar obscuring silhouette. Include exactly one small adult dockworker in practical workwear next to the loading access for scale, and at most two small hand-carry freight cases. Calm, personal, cozy, workaday feel. No written titles, no labels or annotations, no logos, no caption, no watermark. Tiny abstract service markings only.
Constraints: original design; no weapons, no turrets, no military styling, no sweeping aerodynamic wings, no fighter canopy, no flashy neon, no skyscraper-sized vessel. Keep the proposed silhouette visibly distinctive. Concept exploration only, not a purported game screenshot.

concepts.name: Mule
concepts.details: Specific design MULE: a stout compact cab-forward industrial freight vehicle for vacuum, about 14 m long by 6 m wide. Deliberately squared, chamfered silhouette like a pressure-rated work van on landing struts, NOT a smooth capsule. Short upright offset-height cab nose with broad three-pane wraparound cockpit glass; cab floor SAME continuous main deck as the hab, no second storey. Behind it a slightly wider rectangular pressure body containing a compact middle living area and a small rear cargo bay. Squared rear shoulders enclose two modest downward-recessed engines, widely spaced enough for a REAR ramp and cargo hatch between them. Slightly visible hab porthole behind cab, service ribs on roof, small protected antennas, robust four footpads. Warm ivory and muted brick-red color blocks, charcoal machinery and blue shadow. Flat roof, big practical replaceable panels, minimal few bold shapes with fine inset edge seams. Show REAR-LEFT three-quarter so the open rear ramp, modest hold, side living window, and profile of the short front cab all read; a dockworker on the ground by ramp establishes small scale. No oversized truck wheels, no giant containers.

concepts.name: Sidewinder
concepts.details: Specific design SIDEWINDER: a compact asymmetric utility hauler about 14 m long by 7 m wide. Two unequal parallel enclosed volumes joined tightly: on the viewer-facing left a slim rounded pressure cabin running from an inset cockpit at its projecting nose to a warm side hab window; on its right a lower wider squared freight body with a forward-facing short loading ramp. It is a tightly integrated lopsided machine, NOT two separate ships and NOT a cargo container tow vehicle. A substantial enclosed side passage connects living cabin and small cargo bay at midships, all on one deck. The cabin nose projects ~2 m farther forward than the freight hatch, making the signature stepped asymmetric silhouette. Shared full-width mechanical stern with two matching compact engines arranged around the combined center of mass; four low landing legs. Dusty sage-green cabin, warm ivory cargo shell, a restrained yellow-ochre hatch frame, dark muted blue mechanism housings. Very thin ink lines, restrained panel count, tactile access covers and protected pipes. FRONT-left three-quarter, crew next to the short forward cargo ramp. Both volumes remain walkable and plausible, total size like a very small live-in delivery craft rather than a warship.

concepts.name: Kestrel
concepts.details: Specific design KESTREL: a short broad blunt triangular/trapezoidal lifting-body pressure hull, about 13 m long by 8 m wide, with a gently flattened curved roof. NOT a jet, no wings or fins, no pointed fighter nose: the broad wedge itself is the walkable body. A low blunt front face contains three modest separated cockpit windows; central living compartment behind it has an off-center oval skylight and one side porthole. Squared haunches widen toward the rear, housing two compact protected rectangular engine outlets and radiator recesses. A small cargo compartment occupies one rear corner with a visible side hatch and modest ramp, other corner contains machinery. Single full-height walkable deck, low sturdy landing feet, approachable and compact rather than aggressively fast. Main hull muted dusty coral and sun-washed ivory with desaturated petrol-blue underside. Thick shell edges and almost organic rounded corners, minimal roof seams, meticulous tiny latches near removable panels. FRONT-right high three-quarter, view the broad compact form and side ramp; one scale person. Match warm illustrated matte tones and blue-violet shadows with selective fine inkwork.

concepts.name: Cricket
concepts.details: Specific design CRICKET: a very compact twin-pod utility craft about 13 m long by 7.5 m wide, designed as a low affordable space tug converted into a single person's hauler/home. Two short thick octagonal pressure pods sit very close alongside each other, connected by TWO substantial enclosed cross-passages; not thin open trusses. Low forward central cockpit bridge spans the gap and gives a distinctive shallow U-shaped front profile, with modest square windows and useful visibility. One pod is living space with one blue-rimmed hab window; the other is the small cargo compartment with SIDE unloading ramp. The narrow central dorsal channel holds protected utility pipework and a folded radiator, making the roof silhouette unmistakably split. One restrained rear engine at the end of each pod, symmetrical thrust; four compact wide-set articulated landing feet. Short single-deck hulls have fully walkable headroom; it is small enough the dockworker reaches almost halfway up their side. Warm parchment main hull, restrained mustard-yellow pod ends and deep slate-blue bridge, warm lamp by ramp. FRONT-side three-quarter view clearly reveals both closely joined pods, central bridge, and the open side ramp. Refined line art and broad clear color planes, no neon, no weapons, no piles of exterior cargo.
